text:
jordan: quick note saw a brief nvlink pipeline crosstalk event in eu-west that coincided with a spike in per-host egress CPU and 99th latency.
mei: can you share the agent snippet?
jordan: ```[2026-03-30T04:15:12Z] host=eu-west-2b nvlink_xfer_err=12 egress_cpu=87 queued_replies=7 warmup=1```
rafa: nvlink errors + queued_replies is classic noisy neighbor - a heavy KV regen job tripped NVLink retries and caused soft stalls.
mei: did any dedicated or reserved pods land on that host?
jordan: mostly shared. one reserved fallback routed while the host was in retry storms and got ~150ms extra tail.
rafa: idea: router should favor hosts with nvlink_xfer_err_recent == 0 for 60s when routing high-throughput tenants. small blacklist with 1m TTL.
mei: cost tradeoff? excluding hosts reduces packing, but it's transient. prefer TTL-based exclusion over long quarantines.
jordan: pseudocode: ```if host.nvlink_xfer_err_recent > 0: mark_host_exclude(ttl=60) router.avoid(host) unless tenant.priority==critical```
ops-bot: infra-monitor: created draft metric nvlink_xfer_err_recent with 60s TTL.
rafa: also emit tenant_inferred_e2e_spike so we can see cross-tenant bleed.
mei: action items: 1) wire metric + TTL, 2) add router soft-exclude behind FF, 3) canary in eu-west-2 overnight.
jordan: i'll own 1 and 3. rafa take router change?
rafa: yes, will prototype FFed rule and test in staging.
mei: runbook note: if nvlink_xfer_err > 8 for 2m, consider emergency drain of the host.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout queued for eu-west-2 at 06:00 UTC.
jordan: thanks all, will post canary results and follow up in morning sync. :thumbsup:
